children: Flooring manufacturer Mohawk Industries
fell short of the market’s revenue expectations in Q3 2026 as sales only rose 1% year on year to $2.79 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $2.72 per share was 5.4% above analysts’ consensus estimates.
Mohawk Industries (MHK) Q3 2026 highlights:
Revenue
$2.79 billion vs S&P analysts’ estimates of $2.81 billion (1% year-on-year growth, 0.9% miss)
Adjusted EPS
$2.72 vs S&P analysts’ estimates of $2.58 (5.4% beat)
Adjusted EBITDA
$353.4 million vs analyst estimates of $363.5 million (12.7% margin, 2.8% miss)
Adjusted EPS guidance
$1.40 at the midpoint for Q4 2026, below analyst estimates of $1.64
Operating margin
6.7%, up from 5% in the same quarter last year
Market capitalization
$7.86 billion
StockStory’s take

Mohawk Industries’ third quarter was marked by a positive market reaction despite slightly missing Wall Street’s revenue expectations, as management delivered higher non-GAAP profit and improved operating margins. CEO Paul De Cock emphasized that price increases, product mix, and productivity gains helped offset persistent inflation and soft demand, particularly in the U.S. and Europe. He noted that retail and commercial segments outperformed residential construction, with “adoption of our industry-first asthma and allergen-friendly carpet exceeding our expectations,” and highlighted the company’s success in gaining share across multiple product categories amidst a challenging macroeconomic backdrop.

Looking forward, Mohawk’s guidance reflects management’s expectation for continued market weakness and elevated input costs through next year. CFO Nick Manthey explained that the company’s ability to offset cost pressures hinges on a combination of new pricing actions, further product mix improvements, and ongoing productivity initiatives. De Cock added, “Our focus is on outperforming in any market, leading with our innovation and brands, driving operational excellence, and converting profit into cash and turning cash into value per share,” underscoring a commitment to capital discipline and operational rigor.
Key insights from management’s remarks

Management attributed the third quarter’s performance to decisive price actions, targeted product innovation, and improved operational efficiencies, while also outlining a new capital allocation strategy to navigate ongoing market headwinds.
Leadership transition:

Paul De Cock took over as CEO, outlining a four-pillar strategic framework focused on market outperformance, product innovation, operational excellence, and disciplined capital allocation. The transition from former CEO Jeff Lorberbaum was described as seamless, with Lorberbaum remaining as Chairman.
Retail and commercial strength:

While U.S. residential new construction softened, management highlighted relative strength in retail and commercial segments. The company gained share in residential carpet, driven by specialty retail, and saw continued momentum in commercial LVT (luxury vinyl tile) and carpet tiles, especially for office and renovation projects.
Innovation driving share gains:

Adoption of differentiated products—such as asthma- and allergen-friendly carpets and advanced laminate with scratch resistance—supported market share gains. The company’s three global innovation hubs fueled new product development and positive mix shifts.
Proactive inflation management:

Management responded to rising input and energy costs, especially in Europe, by accelerating price increases and cost recovery efforts. The combination of price, mix, and productivity more than offset inflation in most segments, with energy hedging strategies partially mitigating volatility in natural gas markets.
Capital allocation and cash discipline:

The new framework prioritizes high-return organic investments, selective bolt-on acquisitions, and consistent share repurchases. Free cash flow generation was strong, enabling $261 million in share repurchases during the quarter and a new $500 million share buyback authorization, while maintaining low leverage.
Drivers of future performance
Mohawk’s outlook is shaped by expectations of continued market softness, persistent inflation, and a focus on cost controls and capital deployment to support margins and shareholder returns.
Sustained cost pressures:

Management expects mid-single-digit inflation in input and operating costs to persist into early next year, driven by higher energy, raw material, labor, and logistics expenses globally. The company plans to use further price increases, positive product mix, and productivity gains to offset these pressures on a dollar-for-dollar basis.
Disciplined capital allocation:

The newly defined capital allocation framework calls for prioritizing high-return organic investments, maintaining a baseline annual capital expenditure of approximately $375 million, and consistently returning excess capital to shareholders through share repurchases, within a net leverage ceiling of 2x EBITDA.
Portfolio review and operational improvement:

Management has initiated a comprehensive review of all business units to assess market attractiveness, competitive advantage, and cash profitability. Underperforming assets may be repositioned, fixed, or potentially divested, and continued restructuring and productivity initiatives are expected to support margin expansion over time.
Catalysts in upcoming quarters

Moving forward, the StockStory team will be closely watching (1) the pace and impact of new pricing actions and productivity initiatives in offsetting ongoing inflation, (2) evidence of market share gains in higher-value product segments such as specialty retail and commercial LVT, and (3) progress on the company’s portfolio review, including potential asset repositioning or divestitures. Execution on capital allocation discipline and cash generation will also be key signposts for the business.
Mohawk Industries currently trades at $138.54, up from $129.99 just before the earnings. At this price, is it a buy or sell?
